##Shoulder Hit
In the past, this was an unusual play, rarely seen, especially early in the game. It doesn't seem urgent and it isn't sente, but the perception changed when AlphaGo often played it. The idea is to compress Black's position without directly invading. As opposed to an invasion, this play lowers risk and offers a trade of the corner for outside influence. This also fits with the fundamental principle of Go that you don't try to destroy your opponent and get everything, but simply to play better than the opponent so as to get a little more.

Playing a pincer against this shoulder hit is an AI idea that is commonly played. <D:Q9>, <E:R10>, <F:Q10>, and <G:R11> are fixtures in current(2019) professional play but have not quite settled into set patterns yet.
